q: Which statement best describes the relationship between AI, machine learning, and deep learning?
options: Deep learning is the broadest field, containing both AI and machine learning
AI is the broadest field; machine learning is a subset of AI, and deep learning is a subset of machine learning
Machine learning and deep learning are unrelated approaches to building AI
AI is a subset of machine learning, which is a subset of deep learning
explain: AI is the broad field of building systems that perform tasks requiring human-like intelligence. Machine learning is a subset of AI in which systems learn patterns from data instead of following hand-coded rules. Deep learning is a further subset of ML that uses multi-layered neural networks to learn complex patterns.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A bank trains a model on thousands of past loan applications, each labeled "approved" or "denied," so it can predict outcomes for new applications. What type of learning is this?
options: Transfer learning
Reinforcement learning
Unsupervised learning
Supervised learning
explain: Supervised learning uses labeled training data - inputs paired with known correct outputs - so the model learns to predict the label for new, unseen data. The approved/denied labels make this supervised.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A retailer wants to group customers with similar buying habits, but it has no predefined categories. Which machine learning approach fits best?
options: Reinforcement learning
Deep inference
Unsupervised learning
Supervised learning
explain: Unsupervised learning finds structure and groupings in unlabeled data without predefined categories or correct answers. Customer segmentation via clustering is a classic unsupervised use case.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An engineer trains a robot to navigate a warehouse by rewarding it for reaching targets and penalizing it for collisions. This is an example of:
options: Semi-supervised learning
Reinforcement learning
Unsupervised learning
Supervised learning
explain: Reinforcement learning trains an agent through trial and error: it takes actions in an environment and learns from rewards and penalties, gradually discovering the best strategy.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which statement best describes deep learning?
options: A rule-based programming method that replaces machine learning
A subset of machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers to learn complex patterns
A data storage architecture for large datasets
A technique that trains models without any data
explain: Deep learning uses artificial neural networks with multiple (deep) layers. Each layer learns increasingly abstract features, which makes deep learning powerful for images, speech, and language when large datasets are available.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: What is the difference between training and inference in machine learning?
options: Training requires labeled data; inference never uses a trained model
Training is the process of teaching a model from data; inference is using the trained model to make predictions on new data
Training makes predictions; inference updates the model weights
Training and inference are two names for the same process
explain: During training, the model adjusts its internal parameters to learn patterns from data. During inference (deployment), the finished model generates predictions for new inputs without further learning.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: In a house-price prediction model, the square footage and number of bedrooms are the _____, and the sale price is the _____.
options: weights; biases
parameters; hyperparameters
labels; features
features; label
explain: Features are the input variables the model uses to make predictions (square footage, bedrooms). The label is the target value the model is trying to predict (sale price).
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which dataset is appropriate for training a supervised learning model?
options: Raw sensor readings with no outcomes recorded
Customer emails paired with their correct spam or not-spam classification
Images with no descriptions or tags
A collection of unlabeled audio clips
explain: Supervised learning requires labeled data - inputs paired with known outcomes. Emails labeled as spam or not spam provide exactly the input-label pairs a supervised classifier needs.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which of the following is an example of unstructured data?
options: A CSV file of product inventory
A spreadsheet of monthly sales figures
Raw video footage from a security camera
A relational database table of customer records
explain: Unstructured data has no predefined rows-and-columns format - examples include video, audio, images, and free text. Spreadsheets, database tables, and CSV files are structured data.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A model predicts whether an email is spam. If it correctly classifies 95 out of 100 test emails, what is its accuracy?
options: Cannot be determined from this information
explain: Accuracy is the fraction of correct predictions: 95 correct out of 100 total predictions equals 95%.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A model performs extremely well on its training data but poorly on new, unseen data. This problem is called:
options: Regularization
Overfitting
Convergence
Underfitting
explain: Overfitting occurs when a model memorizes the training data - including its noise - instead of learning general patterns, so it fails to generalize to new data. It is typically addressed with more data, simpler models, or regularization.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A model is too simple to capture the underlying pattern in the data, performing poorly on both training and new data. This is:
options: Underfitting
Data leakage
Overgeneralization
Overfitting
explain: Underfitting happens when a model is too simple (or undertrained) to learn the real patterns in the data, so it performs poorly on training data and on new data alike.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which scenario is a classic use case for machine learning?
options: Forecasting future product demand based on historical sales patterns
Storing customer records in a database
Calculating exact payroll taxes using fixed formulas
Sorting a list of names alphabetically
explain: ML excels at learning patterns from historical data to predict future outcomes, such as demand forecasting. Fixed calculations, sorting, and storage are deterministic tasks that do not require learning from data.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A streaming service suggests movies based on what similar users watched. This is an example of:
options: Data encryption
Load balancing
A rules-based firewall
A recommendation system
explain: Recommendation systems use ML to predict what a user will like based on the behavior of similar users or the characteristics of similar items - a core ML use case.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A credit card company flags unusual transactions as potentially fraudulent in real time. Which ML capability does this demonstrate?
options: Speech synthesis
Natural language generation
Image segmentation
Anomaly detection
explain: Fraud detection is a classic anomaly-detection use case: the model learns what normal transaction patterns look like and flags deviations for review.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: What does natural language processing (NLP) enable computers to do?
options: Compress video files
Understand, interpret, and generate human language
Manage network routing tables
Render 3D graphics
explain: NLP is the AI field focused on enabling computers to work with human language - understanding text and speech, and generating language in return.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A model that identifies defective parts on a factory line from camera images is an example of:
options: Database indexing
Natural language processing
Reinforcement learning only
Computer vision
explain: Computer vision enables machines to interpret visual information from images or video. Detecting defects from camera images is a textbook computer vision task.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Predicting a numeric value (such as tomorrow's temperature) is called _____, while predicting a category (such as "rain" or "no rain") is called _____.
options: regression; classification
clustering; regression
classification; regression
inference; training
explain: Regression predicts continuous numeric values (temperature, price). Classification predicts discrete categories or classes (rain vs. no rain, spam vs. not spam).
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Grouping news articles by topic without any predefined topic labels is an example of:
options: Classification
Reinforcement learning
Regression
Clustering
explain: Clustering is an unsupervised technique that groups similar items together. With no predefined topic labels, the algorithm must discover the groupings on its own.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Generally, what effect does increasing the amount of high-quality training data have on an ML model?
options: It makes training faster but less accurate
It always guarantees perfect accuracy DOMAIN 2 - FUNDAMENTALS OF GENERATIVE AI
It has no effect on model performance
It typically improves the model's ability to learn patterns and generalize
explain: More high-quality, representative data generally helps a model learn better patterns and generalize to new examples. Data quality matters as much as quantity, and no amount of data guarantees perfection.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A bank wants to predict which customers are likely to close their accounts, using five years of customer records labeled with whether each customer churned. Which learning method fits?
options: Unsupervised learning
Self-supervised pre-training
Supervised learning
Reinforcement learning
explain: The data is labeled (churned / did not churn) and the goal is to predict a category for new customers. That is supervised learning - specifically classification.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A retailer groups millions of unlabeled transactions to discover natural customer segments for a marketing campaign. Which approach is this?
options: Reinforcement learning
Unsupervised clustering
Supervised classification
Regression
explain: No labels exist and the goal is to find hidden structure (segments). That is unsupervised learning, and grouping similar items is clustering.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An engineer trains a warehouse robot that learns to navigate by receiving positive rewards for successful deliveries and penalties for collisions. This is an example of:
options: Supervised learning
Reinforcement learning
Unsupervised learning
Transfer learning
explain: Learning through trial and error guided by rewards and penalties is the definition of reinforcement learning.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A data scientist sets aside a portion of data to tune hyperparameters and select the best model version before final evaluation. This portion is the:
options: Validation set
Inference set
Test set
Training set
explain: The validation set is used to tune hyperparameters and choose among model versions. The training set teaches the model; the test set is reserved for one final unbiased evaluation.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A model scores 99% accuracy on its training data but only 61% on new, unseen data. This problem is called:
options: Overfitting
Label leakage
Underfitting
Data drift
explain: A large gap between training performance and new-data performance means the model memorized the training data instead of learning general patterns - overfitting.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A company needs fraud scores returned within milliseconds while a transaction is being processed. Which inference type is required?
options: Batch inference
Offline inference
Real-time inference
Federated inference
explain: Millisecond responses during a live transaction require real-time inference via an API endpoint. Batch inference scores large datasets on a schedule instead.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A support ticket classifier assigns each ticket to exactly one category: billing, technical, or account. This is:
options: Regression
Clustering
Multiclass classification
Reinforcement learning
explain: Predicting one of several discrete categories is multiclass classification - a supervised task.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An energy company predicts next month's electricity demand as a single number, based on five years of historical usage data. This task is:
options: Reinforcement learning
Regression
Clustering
Classification
explain: Predicting a continuous numeric value is regression; predicting a category would be classification.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A team has 500 labeled product reviews and 200,000 unlabeled ones. Which approach lets them train a text classifier from this mix?
options: Semi-supervised learning
Supervised learning on the 500 reviews only
Unsupervised clustering only
Reinforcement learning
explain: Semi-supervised learning combines a small labeled set with a large unlabeled set - ideal when labeling is expensive but raw data is plentiful.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A model underfits its training data, performing poorly on both training and new data. Which change is most likely to help?
options: Use a more expressive model with additional relevant features
Train on less data
Remove input features
Add stronger regularization
explain: Underfitting means the model is too simple to capture the pattern - add model capacity or informative features, not regularization.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A data scientist normalizes numeric inputs, removes duplicate rows, and fills missing values before training. This work is:
options: Model deployment
Inference
Hyperparameter tuning
Data preprocessing
explain: Cleaning and preparing raw data - normalization, deduplication, handling missing values - is data preprocessing, and it happens before training begins.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A team uses Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to:
options: Detect drift in deployed models
Build accurately labeled datasets with human reviewers
Deploy models to production endpoints
Run batch inference jobs
explain: SageMaker Ground Truth is a managed data-labeling service that uses human workers (plus machine assistance) to create high-quality labeled training data.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A retailer scores its entire customer base for churn risk in one overnight job every Sunday. This is:
options: Online learning
Real-time inference
Federated learning
Batch inference
explain: Scoring a large dataset on a schedule is batch inference; real-time inference serves one prediction instantly, as during a live transaction.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A data scientist sets the learning rate and batch size before training begins. These are:
options: Hyperparameters
Features
Labels
Parameters
explain: Hyperparameters are configured before training (learning rate, batch size); parameters (weights) are learned by the model during training.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A security team flags employee logins that look nothing like each user's normal behavior, with no labeled examples of attacks. This is:
options: Multiclass classification
Anomaly detection
Reinforcement learning
Regression
explain: Finding rare, unusual patterns without labeled examples is anomaly detection - a classic unsupervised approach for fraud and intrusion use cases.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A fraud model's accuracy falls steadily over six months as criminals change their tactics. This is an example of:
options: Overfitting
Underfitting
Data labeling
Concept drift
explain: Concept drift is when real-world patterns shift after training, degrading the model. Deployed models must be monitored and retrained as the world changes.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A company builds a chatbot that must understand customer intent from typed messages. The ML subfield behind this is:
options: Computer vision
Natural language processing
Reinforcement learning
Time-series forecasting
explain: NLP enables computers to understand and generate human language - the foundation of chatbots, sentiment analysis, and translation.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A startup has thousands of product images but no labels and no budget for labeling. Which method can still find structure in the images?
options: Reinforcement learning
Transfer learning
Unsupervised learning
Supervised classification
explain: Unsupervised learning finds hidden structure (clusters, anomalies) without labels - the right choice when labeling is unavailable or unaffordable.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which best describes a neural network?
options: A clustering algorithm
Layers of interconnected nodes that adjust connection strengths to learn patterns
A database indexing method
A single decision tree
explain: Neural networks are layers of nodes ("neurons") whose connection weights are tuned during training; deep learning stacks many such layers.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A vision model trained mostly on daytime photos performs badly on nighttime images. The most likely root cause is:
options: A low temperature setting
An oversized validation set
Too much regularization
Training data that does not represent real-world conditions
explain: Models only learn what their training data shows them. If the training set doesn't represent real inputs - like nighttime images - the model fails on them.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A hospital uses a voice assistant that can only schedule appointments and answer questions about clinic hours. It cannot diagnose conditions, drive a vehicle, or reason about unrelated topics. This system is best described as which type of AI?
options: Deep learning, because it uses a microphone
General AI, because it understands human speech
Reinforcement learning, because patients reward it with thanks
Narrow AI, because it performs a limited, specific set of tasks well
explain: Narrow AI, also called weak AI, is designed for a specific task or a narrow range of tasks. Appointment scheduling does not transfer to unrelated abilities. General AI would match broad human-like reasoning across domains and is not what deployed narrow systems do.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An education company replaces hand-written if-then rules for essay scoring with a system that improves by studying thousands of graded essays and the scores teachers assigned. What changed about how the system makes decisions?
options: It now uses a deterministic formula for every score
It no longer needs any data to produce a score
It now stores essays in a larger database
It now learns patterns from examples instead of following only explicit rules programmed by developers
explain: Machine learning systems learn patterns from data rather than relying solely on hand-coded rules. Studying graded examples lets the model generalize to new essays. A larger database or a fixed formula alone would not represent learning from examples.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A logistics company feeds years of shipment photos into a neural network with many hidden layers so the system can recognize damaged packaging at increasing levels of detail, from edges to whole-box patterns. Which approach is the company using?
options: A traditional spreadsheet model
Reinforcement learning with rewards for each photo
Clustering with no neural network
Deep learning, a subset of machine learning that uses multi-layered neural networks
explain: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers. Those layers learn progressively more abstract features, which suits image tasks. Merely viewing photos or using rewards does not define this layered-network approach.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A healthcare provider trains a model on past patient records where each case is marked as urgent or non-urgent, then uses it to triage new cases. Which learning type and task type is this?
options: Reinforcement learning and regression
Self-supervised learning and anomaly detection
Unsupervised learning and clustering
Supervised learning and classification, because labeled cases are used to predict a category
explain: The training cases carry a known category, urgent or non-urgent, so the learning is supervised. Predicting a discrete category is classification. Clustering would have no labels, and regression would predict a continuous number instead of a class.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An insurance company trains a model on past policies with driver age, vehicle type, and claims history, where the known total claim cost for each policy is recorded. It wants to predict the expected claim cost for a new policy. Which task type fits best?
options: Classification, because costs are grouped into urgent and non-urgent
Dimensionality reduction, because there are several input fields
Regression, because the target is a continuous dollar amount
Clustering, because no target value is provided
explain: Regression predicts a continuous numeric value such as a dollar amount. The recorded claim cost is the label and the policy details are features. Classification predicts categories, while clustering works without a known target to predict.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which TWO scenarios are examples of supervised learning? (Choose two.)
options: Letting a warehouse robot learn routes purely from trial-and-error rewards with no labeled examples
Training a house-price model on homes with known sale prices
Predicting whether a loan applicant will default, trained on past applicants labeled default or repaid
Grouping shoppers into segments with no predefined segment names
explain: Supervised learning needs labeled examples with known outcomes. Default prediction uses default or repaid labels, and house-price training uses known sale prices. Shopper grouping without predefined names is unsupervised clustering, and trial-and-error route learning is reinforcement learning.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A university has survey responses from 20,000 students but no predefined groups. It wants to discover distinct patterns in study habits so it can tailor support programs. Which approach fits best?
options: Regression using a known satisfaction score for every student
Unsupervised learning using clustering to discover groups in unlabeled data
Speech recognition to transcribe the surveys
Supervised classification using the group names as labels
explain: With no predefined groups or labels, clustering can discover natural groupings in the data. Classification and regression both require a known target for each example, which this university does not have for study-habit segments.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An energy utility monitors grid sensor readings that are normally stable. A model learns the normal pattern and raises an alert when readings deviate sharply with no known fault label attached. Which technique is the model primarily using?
options: Anomaly detection, an unsupervised approach that flags patterns differing from normal behavior
Regression to predict next month's bill
Translation of sensor readings into another language
Classification using labeled fault categories for every reading
explain: Anomaly detection identifies observations that differ significantly from learned normal behavior, which is ideal when fault examples are rare or unlabeled. It differs from classification, which needs labeled examples of each fault category to learn from.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A manufacturing firm collects 500 sensor variables for each machine but wants a simpler representation that keeps most of the useful variation so engineers can visualize machine states in two dimensions. Which technique fits this goal?
options: Real-time inference to score machines faster
Data labeling to add a target value for every sensor
Classification to assign each machine a pass or fail label
Dimensionality reduction to compress many variables into fewer components while retaining key information
explain: Dimensionality reduction reduces the number of input variables while preserving as much meaningful variation as possible, enabling visualization and simpler models. Classification predicts a label and does not by itself compress 500 variables into two dimensions.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A farm deploys a system that adjusts irrigation each day, observing soil moisture and crop response afterward. It receives positive feedback when water use drops without harming yield and negative feedback otherwise, improving its policy over a season. Which learning type is this?
options: Semi-supervised learning from a small labeled dataset
Unsupervised clustering of soil samples
Reinforcement learning, because an agent learns actions from rewards and penalties in an environment
Supervised learning from labeled irrigation photos
explain: Reinforcement learning involves an agent taking actions in an environment and learning from reward signals over time. The irrigation controller is not learning from labeled photos or static groups; it is improving a sequential decision policy from feedback.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A law firm has 300 contracts reviewed and tagged by attorneys and 50,000 untagged contracts. Labeling all of them is too expensive, so the firm wants a method that learns from both sets together. Which approach fits best?
options: Pure unsupervised clustering that ignores the 300 tagged contracts
Reinforcement learning with rewards for each contract read
Batch inference on the tagged contracts only
Semi-supervised learning, which combines a small labeled set with a large unlabeled set
explain: Semi-supervised learning is designed for exactly this situation: a small amount of expensive labeled data plus a large amount of unlabeled data. Ignoring the attorney tags wastes valuable supervision, while pure clustering cannot learn the tag meanings.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A media company pre-trains a model on millions of unlabeled articles by hiding words and asking the model to predict the missing words, creating useful language representations before any task-specific training. Which learning approach is this?
options: Reinforcement learning from viewer ratings
Self-supervised learning, because the model creates its own prediction targets from unlabeled data
Clustering articles into unlabeled groups only
Supervised regression on article prices
explain: In self-supervised learning the supervision signal comes from the data itself, such as predicting masked words or missing parts of an input. No human labels are needed for this pre-training stage, yet the model learns representations useful for later tasks.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A retail team collects product photos and a category name verified by staff for each photo, such as shoes, jackets, or hats. In machine learning terms, what does the verified category name represent?
options: A label, the known correct answer paired with each training example
A feature, because it describes the color of the product
A hyperparameter, because staff chose it before training
An inference endpoint, because it serves predictions
explain: A label is the known target or correct answer attached to a training example. Here the verified category is what a future model should learn to predict from the photo, which serves as the input feature data.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which TWO statements correctly describe labeled and unlabeled data? (Choose two.)
options: Clustering typically requires a label for every record before it can start
Unlabeled data has inputs without a known target, so it is commonly used for clustering and anomaly detection
Unlabeled data always includes a verified outcome for every record
Labeled data pairs each example with a known target that a supervised model can learn to predict
explain: Labeled data includes a known target for each example and supports supervised learning. Unlabeled data lacks that target and is commonly used to find structure through clustering or to model normal behavior for anomaly detection. The other statements reverse these definitions.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A hospital builds a model to predict the likelihood that a patient will be readmitted within 30 days. It uses age, length of stay, and number of prior visits as inputs, and the readmitted-or-not outcome as the target. Which choice correctly identifies the parts?
options: Age and length of stay are labels, and readmission is a feature
Age, length of stay, and prior visits are features, and readmission outcome is the label
Prior visits are the model, and age is the algorithm
All four values are hyperparameters that are set before any data is collected
explain: Features are the input variables used to make a prediction, while the label is the outcome being predicted. Age, stay length, and prior visits are inputs; whether the patient was readmitted is the target label the model learns to predict.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A bank stores account balances, transaction dates, and amounts in relational tables where every row follows the same columns and data types. Which data type is this?
options: Semi-structured data, because it is stored in the cloud
Unstructured data, because bank data is sensitive
Structured data, because it fits a predefined schema of rows and columns
Free-text data, because customers can add memos
explain: Structured data follows a predefined schema with consistent rows, columns, and types, making it easy to query with SQL. Sensitivity or cloud storage does not change the structural category of well-formed relational tables.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A logistics platform stores shipment events as JSON documents. Every event has a shipment ID, but some events include extra fields such as customs notes or temperature readings while others do not. Which data type best describes these records?
options: Semi-structured data, because records share some structure but allow flexible fields, often marked with tags or keys
Labeled data, because the shipment ID is always present
Unstructured data, because JSON cannot be queried at all
Structured data, because every record has identical columns
explain: Semi-structured data has organizational markers such as JSON keys but does not enforce a rigid table schema, so individual records can carry different fields. Whether data is labeled depends on having a prediction target, not on having an ID field.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A hotel chain wants to analyze thousands of free-text guest reviews, recorded support calls, and photos guests uploaded, none of which fit neatly into rows and columns. Which category do these inputs primarily belong to?
options: Structured data
Semi-structured data in every case, because reviews have a star rating attached
Tabular data, because the hotel stores them in a database
Unstructured data, because text narratives, audio, and images lack a predefined row-and-column format
explain: Free text, audio recordings, and images are classic unstructured data because they do not follow a predefined tabular schema. Storing them in a database or attaching a single rating does not convert the narrative, audio, and image content itself into structured data.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A government agency spends three months feeding historical permit applications and their outcomes into a learning algorithm, adjusting the system until its performance on held-back cases is acceptable. Which phase is the agency in?
options: Dimensionality reduction, because the project took three months
Deployment monitoring only, because no learning is occurring
Inference, because citizens are already using the system live
Training, because the model is learning patterns and adjusting its internal parameters from data
explain: Training is the phase where a model learns from data and its internal parameters are adjusted to improve predictions. Inference comes later, when the finished trained model is applied to new inputs without further learning from them.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A real estate website has finished building its home-valuation model. When a visitor enters an address, the website sends the home details to the model and shows an estimated value within a second. What is happening at that moment?
options: Clustering, because the home is grouped with similar homes permanently
Training, because the model relearns from this single home
Inference, because a trained model is generating a prediction for new input data
Labeling, because the visitor is creating training data
explain: Inference is the use of a trained model to generate predictions for new, unseen inputs. The visitor request does not retrain the model; it applies what the model already learned during its earlier training phase.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An insurance company scores its entire book of policies once each night, processing hundreds of thousands of records together when no immediate answer is required. Which inference approach fits this workload?
options: Real-time inference, because each score must return in milliseconds
Reinforcement learning, because the scoring happens overnight
Batch inference, because predictions are generated for many records together on a schedule
Self-supervised learning, because the records have no labels
explain: Batch inference processes large groups of records together at scheduled intervals and tolerates higher latency in exchange for efficiency. Real-time inference is needed only when each individual request requires an immediate response.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which TWO statements correctly contrast batch inference and real-time inference? (Choose two.)
options: Batch inference always returns a result faster for a single urgent request than real-time inference
Real-time inference serves individual requests with low latency as they arrive
Real-time inference can only run once per day on a fixed schedule
Batch inference is well suited to periodic scoring of large volumes of records where immediate answers are not needed
explain: Real-time inference answers individual requests immediately with low latency, while batch inference efficiently scores large volumes on a schedule when immediacy does not matter. The reversed statements confuse the latency and scheduling characteristics of the two modes.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A streaming platform must decide within milliseconds whether a live chat message violates policy before other viewers see it, handling one message at a time as messages arrive. Which inference approach is required?
options: Batch inference run once overnight
Clustering of messages at the end of each week
Offline training on last month's messages
Real-time inference, because each request needs an immediate low-latency prediction
explain: When a decision must be made instantly for each arriving request, real-time inference is required. Batch processing overnight or weekly analysis would deliver the moderation decision long after viewers had already seen the message.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A data science team uses the same learning algorithm twice on two different retail datasets. The resulting systems behave differently because each learned different internal values from its own data. Which statement best explains this?
options: Parameters are set by hand before training and never change during learning
An algorithm is the learning procedure, while a model is the trained result whose learned parameters reflect its specific training data
The algorithm and the model are the same thing, so the datasets must have been identical
Features and labels are interchangeable, so behavior should not differ
explain: An algorithm is the general procedure used to learn, while a model is the concrete artifact produced after training on particular data. Its learned parameters encode patterns from that data, which is why the same algorithm yields different models on different datasets.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A retail demand model finishes training. Analysts inspect the internal numeric values the model adjusted during training to capture how strongly each past promotion affected sales. What are these learned internal values called?
options: Parameters (or weights), the values a model learns during training
Labels, the historical sales figures used only at evaluation time
Algorithms, the step-by-step procedures used to run training
Features, the raw inputs supplied for each new prediction
explain: Parameters, often called weights, are the internal values a model adjusts during training to fit patterns in the data. Features are inputs, labels are target outcomes, and an algorithm is the learning procedure rather than the learned values themselves.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A legal team wants software that reads thousands of contracts, identifies parties, dates, and renewal clauses, and produces a short summary of obligations for each agreement. Which AI capability is central to this task?
options: Computer vision for detecting faces in scanned photos
Forecasting, because renewal dates are in the future
Speech recognition, because contracts are usually spoken aloud
Natural language processing, because the system must understand and summarize human language in text
explain: Extracting entities and summarizing contract text requires NLP capabilities such as entity recognition and summarization. Computer vision might help digitize a scan, but understanding the meaning of the language itself is an NLP task.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: During a televised match, a sports analytics system tracks each player in the video feed, measures sprint speeds, and flags offside positions from camera footage alone. Which AI capability is primarily at work?
options: Speech recognition converting commentary to text
Sentiment analysis of fan comments on social media
Recommendation based on viewer watch history
Computer vision interpreting objects, people, and movement in images and video
explain: Computer vision enables machines to interpret visual content such as people, objects, and movement in video. Tracking players and positions from footage is a vision task, even if other analytics are layered on top afterward.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Physicians dictate visit notes aloud and the system converts their spoken words into text in the medical record, distinguishing different speakers in the room. Which capability does this demonstrate?
options: Image classification of X-ray scans
Text-to-speech generation
Speech recognition, which converts spoken language into written text
Demand forecasting for clinic staffing
explain: Speech recognition, also called speech-to-text, converts spoken audio into text and can include speaker identification. Text-to-speech runs in the opposite direction, turning written text into spoken audio output.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An energy provider uses the past five years of hourly weather and consumption records to estimate electricity demand for each day next week so it can schedule generation. Which ML use case is this?
options: Forecasting, because the company predicts future values from historical time-series patterns
Content moderation, because peak days are flagged as unsafe
Clustering, because days are grouped without any target
Classification only, because demand is reported as high or low
explain: Forecasting predicts future values based on historical time-ordered data. Scheduling generation from predicted daily demand is a classic forecasting use case; the output is a future quantity, not a grouping or a moderation decision.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which TWO elements are typical inputs a recommendation system uses to personalize suggestions? (Choose two.)
options: The number of lines of code in the recommendation service
A user's past ratings, purchases, or viewing behavior
The behavior of similar users whose preferences overlap with this user
The physical temperature of the data center servers
explain: Recommendation systems personalize from signals such as a user's own history and the behavior of similar users, a pattern called collaborative filtering. Server temperature and code size carry no information about what an individual user will prefer.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A streaming service notices that viewers who enjoyed three specific documentaries also tended to enjoy a fourth, so it recommends that fourth title to similar viewers. Which recommendation approach is this?
options: Random selection weighted by title length
Batch inference applied to billing records
Collaborative filtering, because recommendations come from patterns across similar users' behavior
Rule-based filtering written by editors
explain: Collaborative filtering makes recommendations by learning from the collective behavior of many users: people with overlapping tastes receive suggestions based on what similar users liked. No editor-written rule or billing record drives this pattern.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A university deploys an assistant that answers prospective students' typed questions about deadlines, majors, and tuition by understanding the intent behind each question. Which capability is most central?
options: Computer vision for reading campus maps
Anomaly detection on network traffic
Regression for predicting enrollment numbers
Natural language processing for understanding questions and generating appropriate text responses
explain: Understanding the intent and meaning of typed questions and producing relevant text answers is an NLP task. Enrollment prediction would be a separate regression problem and is not what answers each student's question.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Farmers fly drones over orchards and a model examines the leaf images to spot early signs of disease that are hard for the human eye to catch. Which capability is being used?
options: Speech recognition to listen to farm workers
Forecasting to predict next season's rainfall only
Computer vision to analyze images and detect visual patterns associated with disease
Translation to convert crop reports between languages
explain: Analyzing leaf images for visual signs of disease is a computer vision task: the model learns visual patterns from image data. The other options deal with audio, future quantities, or language conversion rather than image interpretation.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A contact center records support calls and automatically produces searchable transcripts, including which agent or customer said each line. Which capability provides the transcripts?
options: Image segmentation that divides call waveforms visually
Speech recognition that converts recorded speech into text with speaker separation
Recommendation systems that suggest help articles
Sentiment scoring that assigns a mood value to each call
explain: Speech recognition converts audio of spoken language into written text, and diarization separates speakers. Sentiment scoring can be applied after transcription, but it does not itself create the transcript from audio.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A retailer wants to predict how many units of a new product will sell next month, expressed as a specific number, using past sales, price, and promotion data. Which problem type should the team frame this as?
options: Regression, because the output is a continuous numeric quantity
Anomaly detection, because next month is unusual
Binary classification, because the answer is yes or no
Clustering, because the answer should be discovered groups
explain: Predicting a specific numeric quantity such as units sold is regression. Classification outputs a category, clustering discovers unlabeled groups, and anomaly detection flags unusual observations rather than estimating an expected sales count.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A government finance office must calculate each citizen's benefit amount using an exact statutory formula where the same inputs must always produce the identical, auditable output. Why is ML a poor fit here?
options: Citizens might submit applications online
The data is stored in relational tables
The task is deterministic with an exact known formula, while ML produces probabilistic approximations that can vary and are harder to audit
ML models are too fast for government systems
explain: ML is a poor fit when an exact, deterministic rule already defines the correct answer, as with a statutory formula. ML outputs are probabilistic estimates learned from data, which undermines the exact reproducibility and auditability this task requires.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A hotel needs to assign housekeeping tasks each morning using a fixed policy: suites are cleaned first, then occupied rooms, then vacant rooms, exactly as written in its operations manual. What is the most appropriate solution?
options: A simple rules-based program that follows the stated priority exactly
A reinforcement learning agent that experiments with guest rooms
A deep learning model trained on years of cleaning photos
A recommendation system trained on guest reviews
explain: When requirements are simple, fixed, and fully specified in advance, a rules-based program is cheaper, exact, and easier to maintain than ML. Training a learning model adds cost and unpredictability without solving any pattern-recognition problem.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which TWO scenarios are poor fits for machine learning? (Choose two.)
options: Sorting employee records alphabetically by last name for a directory
Computing an invoice total by adding line items and applying a fixed tax rate
Grouping news readers into interest segments from unlabeled browsing data
Predicting customer churn from thousands of historical accounts with known outcomes
explain: Invoice totals and alphabetical sorting are deterministic tasks with exact procedures that need no learning from data. Churn prediction from labeled history and segment discovery from unlabeled behavior are both strong ML fits because the patterns must be learned.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A clinic wants an ML model to predict an extremely rare condition, but it can provide only four confirmed historical cases and no other relevant data. What is the MOST significant problem with this plan?
options: The predictions would need real-time inference
The clinic's data is semi-structured instead of structured
There is far too little training data for a model to learn reliable patterns and generalize
The condition is too rare for doctors to describe
explain: ML models learn statistical patterns, and a handful of examples cannot support reliable generalization, especially for a rare and variable condition. More representative data or a different approach, such as expert rules, would be needed first.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A logistics company processes thousands of handwritten delivery forms daily. The handwriting varies widely, no fixed template rules work reliably, and the company has years of forms paired with verified transcriptions. Why is ML a good fit here?
options: Because the forms can be sorted alphabetically instead
Because ML guarantees perfect transcription of every form
Because handwriting follows a single exact formula
Because the pattern is complex, varies across examples, and large amounts of labeled examples are available to learn from
explain: ML excels when the mapping is too complex and variable for hand-written rules but large volumes of labeled examples exist to learn from. Handwriting recognition fits that profile, though ML still does not guarantee perfection on every example.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A streaming service defines its business problem as deciding, for each subscriber, whether they will cancel in the next 30 days: yes or no. Which ML problem type has the team defined?
options: Regression, because cancellation is measured in days
Clustering, because subscribers fall into natural groups
Classification, because the outcome is one of a set of discrete categories
Dimensionality reduction, because many viewing features exist
explain: A yes-or-no cancellation outcome is a discrete category, so this is binary classification. The 30-day window defines the prediction horizon, but the predicted value itself is a class, not a continuous number of days.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A courier company wants to estimate the delivery time in minutes for each new parcel based on distance, traffic, and depot workload. Which ML problem type is this?
options: Clustering, because routes form geographic groups
Regression, because delivery time is a continuous numeric value to predict
Anomaly detection, because late deliveries are unusual
Classification, because parcels are labeled delivered or not
explain: Estimating minutes, a continuous quantity, is a regression task even though delivery data also contains categories. Classification would predict a discrete outcome, and clustering would group parcels without predicting a specific time.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A real estate firm wants to understand its buyer market by finding natural groupings among past inquiries, with no group names defined in advance and no outcome to predict. Which ML problem type fits?
options: Regression to predict each buyer's budget exactly
Clustering, because the goal is to discover groups in unlabeled data
Classification using the group names as training labels
Forecasting next quarter's total inquiry volume
explain: Clustering discovers structure in unlabeled data when no target or predefined groups exist. Classification would require labeled group examples, and regression or forecasting predict numeric values rather than revealing market segments.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A factory already has a classifier for common labeled fault types, but engineers also need a system that alerts them to entirely new vibration patterns never seen or labeled before. Why does anomaly detection fit this second need better than classification?
options: Anomaly detection needs labeled examples of every new fault first
Anomaly detection models normal behavior and flags deviations, so it can surface novel patterns that a classifier trained on known classes would miss or force into a known category
Anomaly detection runs without any input data
Classification can predict fault types it was never trained on
explain: A classifier can only assign inputs to classes it learned during training, so novel faults get misclassified as known ones. Anomaly detection instead learns what normal looks like and flags deviations, making unknown failure modes visible to engineers.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An agriculture team wants to train a supervised yield-prediction model across many farms. Which dataset requirement is essential before training begins?
options: The model must be deployed for inference before any data is gathered
Each historical field record must include the actual harvested yield as the label alongside its soil and weather features
The records must contain no outcome information at all
Only unlabeled satellite images are needed, with no measured yields
explain: Supervised learning requires examples where the target outcome is known. Historical fields need measured yields as labels paired with soil and weather features; without outcomes, the model has nothing to learn the prediction mapping from.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which TWO statements about inference are correct? (Choose two.)
options: Real-time inference returns a prediction for a single request with low latency
Inference updates a model's parameters using training data
Batch inference can process a large set of stored records together at a scheduled time
Inference is only performed before a model is trained
explain: Inference applies a trained model to generate predictions. It can run in batch mode over many stored records on a schedule or in real-time mode for single low-latency requests. Updating parameters describes training, not inference.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A school district generates predicted reading-support needs for every student once a week from updated assessment data, and counselors review the lists on Monday mornings. Which inference mode best matches this workflow and minimizes unnecessary cost?
options: Reinforcement learning that revises predictions hourly
Batch inference run weekly over all student records
Real-time inference with an always-on endpoint for each student
No inference, because predictions are only made during training
explain: The predictions are needed on a weekly cadence for the full student population, not instantly per request, so scheduled batch inference fits and avoids paying for a continuously available low-latency endpoint that nobody queries in real time.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A hospital monitoring system must alert clinicians within seconds when a patient's vital signs suggest rapid deterioration, evaluating each new reading as it arrives. Which inference mode is required and why?
options: Offline inference after discharge, because trends are clearer then
Batch inference, because accuracy matters more than speed
Real-time inference, because each arriving reading needs an immediate prediction so staff can act without delay
Weekly batch scoring, because readings accumulate over time
explain: Clinical deterioration demands an immediate response to each new reading, which is the defining use case for real-time inference. Any scheduled or retrospective batch approach would surface the alert after the window for effective intervention.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A bank's data team explains that linear regression is the method they will use to learn from lending data, and the deployed credit-scoring artifact is what that method produces after learning. Which pairing is correct?
options: The algorithm is a feature, and the model is a label
Linear regression is the model, and the scoring artifact is the algorithm
Both terms refer to the raw lending data itself
Linear regression is the algorithm (learning procedure), and the trained scoring artifact is the model
explain: The algorithm is the learning procedure, such as linear regression, while the model is the trained artifact that procedure produces from data and that is later deployed for predictions. Data, features, and labels are separate concepts from both.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Before training a support-ticket routing model, an engineer sets the learning rate and the maximum depth the model is allowed to use. During training, the model itself adjusts its internal weights. Which statement is correct?
options: Hyperparameters are the predictions the model makes on new tickets
Learning rate and depth are labels taken from the tickets
The learning rate and depth are hyperparameters set by people, while the weights are parameters learned by the model during training
Weights are set by hand before training and never change
explain: Hyperparameters are configuration choices set by practitioners before training, such as learning rate and maximum depth. Parameters, or weights, are the internal values the learning process adjusts automatically as it fits the training data.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A census bureau publishes results as tables where each row is a household and each column is a defined field such as household size and income bracket. A researcher wants to know which data category this published table represents.
options: Structured data, because it follows a fixed schema of rows and defined columns
Unlabeled data, because households are anonymous
Unstructured data, because census topics are complex
Semi-structured data, because it was published on a website
explain: A table with a fixed schema of rows and defined columns is structured data regardless of topic complexity or where it is published. Anonymity relates to privacy, not to whether the data follows a predefined structure.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An insurer lists the inputs for a premium model: driver age, years licensed, vehicle safety rating, and annual mileage. The premium amount itself is what the model must predict. Which statement is correct?
options: The premium is a feature and the four inputs are labels
Driver age is the algorithm and mileage is the model
Driver age, years licensed, safety rating, and mileage are features, and the premium is the label
All five values are unstructured data
explain: Features are the measurable inputs a model uses, and the label is the value it predicts. The four driver and vehicle attributes feed the prediction, while the premium amount is the target outcome the model learns to estimate.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A warehouse stores 100,000 camera images of shelves, but nobody has recorded what each image contains or whether shelves were stocked correctly. Which term describes this dataset?
options: Training labels, because the warehouse intends to use them later
Labeled data, because the images were captured on a schedule
Unlabeled data, because the images have no associated target or annotation
Structured data, because cameras produce files of equal size
explain: Data is unlabeled when examples have no associated target, annotation, or known outcome attached. The images could later be labeled for supervised learning or used as-is for unsupervised methods, but capture schedule and file size do not create labels.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A hospital can afford expert labeling for only 400 pathology slides, but it holds 80,000 unlabeled slides. An ML engineer proposes a method that first learns tissue structure from all slides and then refines decisions using the 400 labeled ones. Why is semi-supervised learning attractive here?
options: It guarantees the same accuracy as labeling all 80,000 slides
It leverages a large unlabeled collection together with a small labeled set, reducing dependence on expensive expert labeling while still learning the target distinction
It removes the need for any labeled examples at all
It converts the slides into structured tables automatically
explain: Semi-supervised learning extracts value from abundant unlabeled data while a small labeled set anchors the actual task, which fits costly expert labeling. It does not eliminate labels entirely or guarantee parity with fully labeled training.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A retailer pre-trains a model on millions of unlabeled product descriptions by masking a word in each description and requiring the model to recover it. No employee creates labels for this stage. Which approach is this and what makes it possible?
options: Clustering, because descriptions are grouped by category afterward
Reinforcement learning, because masked words act as rewards
Supervised learning, because employees wrote the descriptions
Self-supervised learning, because the correct masked word is derived from the data itself, giving a training signal without human labels
explain: Self-supervised learning constructs the target from the input itself, here the masked word, so unlabeled data still provides a learning signal. Human authorship of the raw text is not labeling, and no external reward or grouping defines this pre-training task.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A city traffic system observes congestion, chooses signal timing changes, and later measures whether traffic flow improved or worsened, using that outcome to refine future timing choices. Which components of reinforcement learning are present?
options: Embeddings, tokens, and a context window
Clusters, centroids, and distance metrics
An agent (the traffic system), an environment (city traffic), actions (timing changes), and rewards based on resulting flow
Features, labels, and a training-test split
explain: Reinforcement learning needs an agent interacting with an environment by taking actions and receiving rewards that reflect outcomes. The traffic system matches all four elements; the other option sets belong to supervised learning, generative models, and clustering.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A translation app converts text between Spanish and English very accurately but cannot answer questions, recognize images, or perform any task outside translation. How should this app be classified?
options: Narrow AI, because it excels at one specific task without general intelligence across domains
General AI, because language involves complex reasoning
A foundation model, because it works in two languages
Unsupervised learning, because users type freely
explain: Capability limited to a single well-defined task is narrow AI, regardless of how sophisticated that task is. General AI would imply broad, human-like ability to learn and perform many different kinds of tasks, which this app does not have.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A technology executive describes a hypothetical future system that could learn any intellectual task a human can, transferring knowledge freely between medicine, law, engineering, and art without being built for each one. Which concept is being described?
options: Batch inference across many departments
Deep learning with extra hidden layers
General AI (AGI), a hypothetical broad intelligence that does not describe today's deployed task-specific systems
Narrow AI applied to many separate products
explain: General AI, or AGI, refers to a hypothetical system with broad, human-like ability to learn and transfer knowledge across arbitrary domains. Today's deployed systems are narrow, built and trained for specific tasks even when they are very capable within them.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A media company must choose a technique for analyzing millions of hours of video and audio to detect scenes, speakers, and topics. A consultant recommends deep learning over a simple model. Which justification is MOST accurate?
options: Deep learning always outperforms every other method on small tabular datasets
Deep learning excels at learning complex patterns from very large amounts of unstructured data such as images, audio, and text
Deep learning is the only method that can run inference in the cloud
Deep learning needs no training data, which suits a large media archive
explain: Deep learning's strength is learning hierarchical patterns from large volumes of complex, unstructured data like video, audio, and text. It still requires substantial training data, and simpler models often remain better for small, well-structured tabular problems.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A sports streaming service automatically tags each uploaded highlight as basketball, soccer, tennis, swimming, or boxing so fans can filter by sport. Which problem type is this?
options: Multi-class regression, because highlights have a duration in seconds
Dimensionality reduction to two visual components
Binary clustering with five labels supplied in advance
Multi-class classification, because each highlight is assigned to one category from a defined set of more than two classes
explain: Assigning each item to one category from a defined set is classification, and with five possible sports it is multi-class classification. The duration being numeric does not make the tagging task regression, since the predicted output is the sport category.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which TWO techniques are forms of unsupervised learning? (Choose two.)
options: Training a price regressor on homes with known sale prices
Dimensionality reduction that compresses sensor variables into fewer components
Training a churn classifier on accounts labeled churned or retained
Clustering customers into segments without predefined labels
explain: Clustering and dimensionality reduction are unsupervised because they find structure in data without a labeled target. The churn classifier and price regressor both learn from known outcomes, which makes them supervised learning.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A landlord analytics tool predicts a monthly rent figure for a listing based on square footage, neighborhood, and number of bathrooms. Midway through the project, a stakeholder asks why the team is not reporting results as simply high or low. What is the best response?
options: The team chose regression because the required output is a specific continuous rent amount, while classification would only assign a category such as high or low
The stakeholder is right; every numeric input forces a classification model
Regression and classification produce identical outputs, so the choice was arbitrary
The team should switch to clustering because rents form neighborhood groups
explain: The deliverable is a specific dollar amount, a continuous value, which is the definition of a regression task. Classification would discard precision by returning only a category, which does not meet the stated requirement for an actual rent figure.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Two analysts work with the same student dataset. Analyst A groups students by similar course-taking patterns without any outcome in mind. Analyst B predicts which students will fail a course using past students with known pass and fail outcomes. Which comparison is correct?
options: Analyst A is doing regression and Analyst B is doing clustering
Neither task involves machine learning because student data is structured
Analyst A is doing unsupervised clustering, while Analyst B is doing supervised classification because known pass and fail labels guide learning
Both analysts are doing supervised classification
explain: Grouping by similarity with no target is unsupervised clustering. Predicting a pass or fail category using historical examples with known outcomes is supervised classification. Structured data is routinely used for ML, so the last option is incorrect.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A customer support assistant has already been trained and deployed. A customer submits a new question and receives an answer a moment later. A manager asks whether the assistant is training at that moment. What is the correct explanation?
options: No, the assistant is performing batch training on all questions at once
Only if the customer rates the answer with a star
Yes, every customer question fully retrains the assistant
No, the deployed assistant is performing inference: applying its previously learned patterns to a new input without retraining on it
explain: A deployed system answering a new question is performing inference with the model it already has. Retraining is a separate, deliberate process using training data; a single live question does not rebuild the model in normal operation.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A shipping company computes risk scores for all next-day routes. Scores are needed by 6 AM, the computation is heavy, and no score is ever requested interactively. An architect proposes a real-time endpoint. What is the BEST assessment?
options: Training must run every hour instead of inference
The company should abandon scoring because batch results arrive after midnight
Batch inference is the better fit because the workload is predictable, bulk, and deadline-based, so an always-on real-time endpoint adds cost without benefit
Real-time inference is required because the scores involve geography
explain: Inference mode should follow the access pattern. A bulk, scheduled, deadline-driven workload is the textbook case for batch inference; paying for continuous low-latency serving that no one calls interactively wastes money without improving outcomes.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which THREE are examples of unstructured data? (Choose three.)
options: A free-form product review paragraph
A photograph of a delivered package
A relational table with fixed columns for order ID, date, and amount
A customer service call recording
explain: Audio recordings, free-form narrative text, and photographs lack a predefined row-and-column structure and are classic unstructured data. A relational table with fixed columns is structured data, which is why it is the one option that does not belong.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An insurer notices that fraudulent claim patterns keep shifting as fraudsters adapt, and analysts cannot write stable rules that stay accurate for long. The insurer has millions of historical claims with investigated outcomes. Why does ML fit this problem?
options: Because regulators require all insurers to use deep learning
Because ML can learn complex, evolving patterns from large volumes of labeled historical data and be retrained as patterns change
Because claim amounts are stored in a database table
Because ML produces the same fixed answer forever once deployed
explain: ML fits problems where patterns are complex and change over time and where large labeled datasets exist to learn from, with retraining keeping pace as behavior shifts. Fixed hand-written rules degrade quickly against adaptive adversaries for exactly this reason.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A state agency must determine eligibility for a benefit by applying exact income thresholds published in law, where any deviation from the prescribed calculation is a legal error. An official proposes replacing the calculation with an ML model trained on past decisions. What is the strongest objection?
options: The model's training would take place in the cloud
Past decisions are stored electronically, which blocks ML
The task requires exact, reproducible application of a known rule, while an ML model gives probabilistic approximations that can deviate from the legal standard and create unlawful outcomes
Eligibility affects too few people to justify any software
explain: When the correct answer is fully defined by an exact rule, ML's probabilistic approximations introduce avoidable legal risk and inconsistency. A deterministic implementation of the published thresholds is auditable and always produces the legally prescribed result.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Attorneys want a tool that scans merger agreements and pulls out the names of the companies involved, the effective dates, and the governing law mentioned in each document. Which NLP capability directly provides these extracted items?
options: Topic clustering of unlabeled documents with no extraction goal
Named entity recognition, which identifies and classifies entities such as organizations, dates, and locations in text
Image upscaling to sharpen scanned pages
Speech synthesis, which reads the agreement aloud
explain: Named entity recognition is the NLP technique that finds and classifies specific entities in text, exactly matching the need to pull company names, dates, and similar items from agreements. Reading aloud or sharpening images does not extract the entities.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which TWO business problems involve both a defined ML problem type and a suitable inference mode? (Choose two.)
options: Forecasting monthly electricity usage for every meter with a batch run at month end
Calculating sales tax with a fixed statutory rate during checkout
Alphabetizing a staff directory once for publication
Classifying support tickets as urgent or routine in real time as each ticket is submitted
explain: Ticket triage is real-time classification and meter usage forecasting is batch regression or forecasting, both pairing a genuine ML problem with a matching inference mode. Tax calculation and alphabetizing are deterministic procedures that need no ML at all.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A research lab records gene expression across 20,000 measurements per sample, making analysis slow and visualization impossible. The team compresses each sample into a small set of components that retain most of the variation between samples. Which technique did the team apply and why?
options: Clustering, because samples now have group assignments only
Dimensionality reduction, because it reduces the number of variables while preserving most of the information needed for analysis and visualization
Regression, because 20,000 is a large number
Anomaly detection, because unusual genes were removed as errors
explain: Dimensionality reduction transforms many variables into a compact representation that preserves the dominant structure of the data, enabling faster analysis and plotting. It does not merely assign groups or discard unusual values as errors.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A boutique hotel chain suggests spa bookings, restaurants, and excursions to each guest based on what that guest enjoyed on previous stays and what similar guests booked. Which system is the chain operating?
options: A recommendation system that personalizes suggestions from guest history and similar-guest behavior
A speech recognition system for front-desk calls
A document extraction system for invoices
A forecasting system for next year's room rates
explain: Personalized suggestions derived from a user's own history and the behavior of similar users are the hallmark of a recommendation system. The other systems forecast quantities, transcribe speech, or extract document fields rather than personalizing offers.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A solar farm operator uses weather forecasts and the past year of hourly generation records to estimate how much power the farm will produce each hour tomorrow. Which use case is this?
options: Time-series forecasting of a future numeric output from historical patterns
Classification of panels into working or broken categories
Speech recognition applied to maintenance logs
Clustering of days with similar cloud cover and no target
explain: Estimating future hourly generation from historical time-ordered records is time-series forecasting: the model predicts a numeric value for a future time period. The goal is a future quantity, not a category, grouping, or transcription.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An engineering lead notes that building the churn model took two days of computing on historical data, yet each live prediction now returns in a fraction of a second for a single customer. Which statement explains this difference?
options: Live predictions are batch jobs that wait for thousands of customers
Inference is always more expensive than training for every model
The model relearns from scratch for every live prediction
Training is a heavier, periodic process that learns parameters from a full dataset, while inference is a lighter per-request application of the finished model
explain: Training processes an entire dataset repeatedly to learn model parameters, which is computationally heavy but done periodically. Inference applies the finished model to one new input, which is comparatively light and fast enough for interactive use.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A retailer wants shoppers to see a compatibility check the moment they add a part to their cart, using a model hosted behind an API that returns a yes-or-no answer per request. Which concept describes the shopper-facing moment when the model answers?
options: Labeling, because the shopper supplies the answer
Clustering, because parts are grouped by category
Inference through a real-time endpoint, because a trained model serves a prediction for a single new request on demand
Training, because parameters change with each cart
explain: Serving a prediction for a single new request on demand is real-time inference through an endpoint. The model's parameters do not change per cart, and the shopper is receiving a prediction, not labeling training data or grouping parts.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: A diagnostics startup has 250 expert-labeled scans and 120,000 unlabeled scans for a condition where labeling costs about $200 per scan. It needs the strongest practical model without labeling the full archive, and it can validate results carefully before any clinical use. Which strategy is BEST aligned with the learning types involved?
options: Use only unsupervised clustering and report the clusters as confirmed diagnoses
Combine self-supervised pre-training on the unlabeled scans to learn image structure with supervised fine-tuning on the 250 labeled scans to learn the diagnostic distinction
Discard the unlabeled scans and train only on 250 examples, accepting severe data scarcity
Label all 120,000 scans first, regardless of cost, because no method can use unlabeled scans
explain: This pairs the strengths of both paradigms: self-supervised pre-training extracts representations from abundant unlabeled images at no labeling cost, and supervised fine-tuning on the small labeled set teaches the actual diagnostic task. Using only 250 examples wastes the archive, and clusters alone are not validated diagnoses.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: An emergency network needs a system that, for each arriving patient, instantly estimates the probability of sepsis, a yes-or-no clinical event, so staff can prioritize care. The team must frame both the problem type and the inference mode correctly. Which framing is correct?
options: Regression with batch inference, because probabilities are numbers reviewed weekly
Dimensionality reduction with real-time inference, because vital signs are numerous
Binary classification with real-time inference, because the event is a discrete outcome and each patient needs an immediate probability as they arrive
Clustering with batch inference, because patients naturally form groups overnight
explain: Sepsis-or-not is a discrete outcome, so estimating its probability is binary classification, and the clinical need for an instant score on arrival requires real-time inference. Batch review or grouping patients would delay the prioritization the system exists to provide.
domain: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

q: Which TWO scenarios are strong fits for machine learning? (Choose two.)
options: Translating a fixed legal disclaimer using a word-for-word table mandated by regulators
Adding two numbers on a checkout receipt
